Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Planned non-blocking kernel rotation in westus5 — customer advisory

Hello Marcus / Stellar infra team,

We're planning a targeted, non-blocking kernel and IO-driver rotation in westus5 on Saturday, 2026-10-10. This is a scheduled maintenance to address an upstream kernel compatibility issue that can cause rare tail-latency spikes on long-lived inference sessions. Key points: 

- Window: 2026-10-10 00:00 — 12:00 UTC (we will perform staggered operations across node groups; each node group will see a ~90–120 minute window).
- Impact: We expect no customer-visible downtime. Operations will be staged with KV cache warmup and rolling restarts; any in-progress requests will be drained gracefully.
- Exclusion option: We can exclude specific clusters (e.g., cluster-b) if you have critical batch windows — please confirm below.
- Monitoring & rollback: We'll run a canary on a small fleet first, then roll forward. If anomalies appear, we will pause and rollback to the previous kernel variant.

Attachments: westus5-maintenance-runbook.pdf (runbook + rollback steps), westus5-impact-matrix.csv (customer-facing impact matrix). Also referenced: https://redwood.status.page/westus5-maintenance (live updates) and INF-8321 in our Jira.

Ask: please confirm by EOD PT whether we need to exclude any clusters or blackout periods. If we don't hear back we'll proceed with the plan and exclude none.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Site Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0142

Subject: Re: Planned non-blocking kernel rotation in westus5 — customer advisory

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the heads up. Two quick items from our side: 

1) Please avoid touching cluster-b (westus5-cluster-b) between 00:00—06:00 UTC on 2026-10-10. We have nightly ETL batch jobs that cannot be interrupted.
2) Can you confirm how KV cache warmup is preserved across the rotation? We rely on warm KV caches for sub-50ms tail latencies for a subset of sessions.

If you can run the canary earlier (even in the previous day UTC window) against a representative serve pool that would help.

Marcus
Marcus Lee
Head of Infrastructure, Stellar Data
mlee@stellardata.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lee <mlee@stellardata.com>, infraops@stellardata.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned non-blocking kernel rotation in westus5 — customer advisory

Hi Marcus — thanks for the quick reply. Confirming we will exclude westus5-cluster-b from the 00:00—06:00 UTC subwindow on 2026-10-10. We'll schedule the canary earlier on 2026-10-09 18:00 UTC against a representative shard pool and share telemetry.

KV cache preservation: our flow will: 
- Do an in-place kernel update on a small canary group and run synthetic traffic to warm KV caches.
- For the rolling groups, we use prefix-preserving drain + snapshot of hot KV entries; during restart the runtime populates cache from the snapshot and from a transient warm-replay to avoid cold-start spikes. In practice, this keeps 95th percentile latencies within the current SLO for long-lived sessions. Full details are in the attached runbook (section 3.2).

If the canary shows degradation we'll pause and perform a controlled rollback. We'll also publish a short post-maintenance note with per-cluster latency deltas.

I'll post the canary telemetry link as soon as it's available (expected within 90 minutes of the canary run).

Best,
Soojin
